name: assert_get
prose: int assert_get(int argc, char **argv) in libfido2 tools/assert_get.c (lines 211-328; the packet called it main, but the enclosing function is assert_get, called with the sub-command's argc/argv). Postcondition: it parses the options -b, -d, -h, -i <file>, -o <file>, -p, -r, -t <toggle>, -u, -v and -w with getopt (any other option calls usage()); after the options, usage() is called if no device argument remains. It opens the input and output files, calls fido_init, builds the assertion with prepare_assert, opens the device named by argv[0] (forcing U2F when -u was given), and, if the pin option is true, prompts with readpassphrase and requires a PIN of 4 to 63 characters, then calls fido_dev_get_assert (with the PIN or NULL); the PIN buffer is cleared afterwards. With -r it prints every assertion in the result, otherwise it requires exactly one assertion and prints it. It then closes and frees the device and assertion, closes both files and calls exit(0), so it does not return. Failures (snprintf error, readpassphrase failure, bad PIN length with the PIN buffer cleared first, fido_dev_get_assert not FIDO_OK, assertion count not 1 without -r) end the process through errx(1, ...), and usage() also ends the process.
note: slice cut head; the function is assert_get (line 212), not main; the helpers (open_read, open_write, prepare_assert, open_dev, usage) were not read

name: pcapint_filter_with_aux_data
prose: u_int pcapint_filter_with_aux_data(const struct bpf_insn *pc, const u_char *p, u_int wirelen, u_int buflen, const struct pcap_bpf_aux_data *aux_data) (libpcap bpf_filter.c lines 85-386; slice cut head). Precondition: pc is NULL or a program accepted by pcapint_validate_filter (the interpreter does not check scratch-memory indices, jump targets, constant divide or shift operands, or that the program ends in a return), p points to at least buflen readable bytes. Postcondition: returns (u_int)-1 if pc is NULL (accept everything). Otherwise it runs the program from the first instruction, with A = X = 0, until a return instruction: BPF_RET|BPF_K returns pc->k and BPF_RET|BPF_A returns A (both as u_int). It returns 0 early when a packet load (absolute word/half/byte, indirect word/half/byte, or the BPF_MSH load) would read outside the first buflen bytes (this also covers an absolute byte load with an ancillary SKF_AD offset other than the VLAN ones, which is simply treated as a large offset), when a VLAN tag ancillary load is requested and aux_data is NULL (only in builds that define SKF_AD_VLAN_TAG_PRESENT), and when BPF_DIV or BPF_MOD by the X register finds X == 0. Shifts by X of 32 or more give 0. An unrecognised opcode calls abort(). The scratch memory array is local and uninitialised until written.
note: reviewer R15 (unsupported SKF_AD loads return 0) is covered: they fall to the default case and fail the k >= buflen check; R1 (runtime out-of-bounds returns 0) RIGHT

name: bpf_image
prose: char *bpf_image(const struct bpf_insn *p, int n) (libpcap bpf_image.c lines 129-424; slice cut head). Precondition: p points to a readable instruction; n is the instruction's index. Postcondition: returns a pointer to a static buffer image[256] declared 'static thread_local', formatted by snprintf as '(NNN) mnemonic operand' where NNN is n in three digits; for the opcodes handled by the switch the mnemonic and operand text come from p->k (immediate, absolute or indirect load offset, memory slot, jump target n+1+k for JA, or 'x' or empty for the register forms; absolute loads of Linux ancillary offsets are printed symbolically when known), and for any other opcode the mnemonic is 'unimp' with the raw code in hex. For conditional jumps (BPF_JMP other than JA) the line also ends with 'jt n+1+jt jf n+1+jf'. The buffer is overwritten by the next call in the same thread. thread_local expands to _Thread_local (C11), a compiler-specific thread-local keyword, or, only for compilers where none is available (TinyCC), to nothing; so the buffer is per-thread in the normal case and the function is not thread-safe only in the fallback case.
note: reviewer R15 (buffer shared across threads) WRONG in the normal case: static thread_local (bpf_image.c:133) with thread_local defined in thread-local.h:50-61 as per-thread storage; shared only under __TINYC__

name: print_debug
prose: static void print_debug(void *this_fn, void *call_site, action_type action) in libpcap instrument-functions.c (lines 70-248). Postcondition: on the first call it reads INSTRUMENT: unset or empty turns instrumentation off for all later calls; 'global' or 'g' selects global-only filtering; 'all' or 'a' is accepted; any other value prints a message on stderr and calls exit(1). With instrumentation off it returns at once. On the first active call (abfd still NULL) it locates the executable through /proc/self/exe and sets up BFD; readlink failure (message by perror), a possibly truncated path (message printed on stdout), bfd_openr failure, bfd_check_format failure, symbol table size or canonicalisation failure, or a missing .text section prints a message (BFD ones through bfd_perror) and returns; the failures before bfd_openr succeeds leave abfd NULL so the setup is retried on the next call, but later failures leave abfd set, so later calls skip the setup and use a symbol table or text section that was not initialised. In global mode it searches the symbol table for this_fn and, if found with a type other than 'T', returns silently. Otherwise, if this_fn is below the .text address it prints '[ERROR address this_fn]' (with no newline), or, if bfd_find_nearest_line fails for it, prints '[ERROR bfd_find_nearest_line this_fn]' (no newline); in both cases profile_func_level is not changed. On success it increments profile_func_level first for ENTER, prints indentation, '[>> ' or '[<< ', the function name or '???' and the level in parentheses; for an ENTER of a function not named 'main' it appends the caller's function, file and line (or an error marker) in the ' from ...' form; it ends the line with a newline and, for EXIT, decrements profile_func_level afterwards. It flushes stdout at the end, except on the silent returns.
note: reviewers RIGHT (R15): truncation message goes to stdout, BFD failures print messages, and only the early failures (readlink/truncation/bfd_openr) are retried; R1 (silent global-filter return; level not always adjusted) RIGHT

name: getopt
prose: int getopt(int nargc, char * const *nargv, const char *ostr) (libpcap missing/getopt.c lines 58-132). Precondition: nargc >= 1, nargv holds nargc valid strings, ostr is a string of option letters (a ':' after a letter means it takes an argument); the function keeps its scanning position in the file-static 'place' and the program name in a static, and uses the globals optind, optopt, optarg, opterr and optreset. It reads opterr and optind, and modifies optind, optopt, optarg and place, and clears optreset when it was set. Postcondition: returns -1 (without setting optarg) when optind >= nargc or the current element does not begin with '-' (place is reset, optopt unchanged), when the element is '--' (optind advances past it, optopt unchanged), or when the scanned letter is '-' and '-' is not in ostr (optopt becomes '-', optind is not advanced even if the element is exhausted; a lone '-' ends the options this way). It returns '?' for the letter ':' or a letter not in ostr (optopt set to that letter; optind advances if the element is exhausted; a diagnostic goes to stderr when opterr is non-zero and ostr does not start with ':'; optarg is not changed). For a letter that takes an argument it sets optarg to the rest of the same element or else the next element and advances optind past them; if there is no next element it advances optind, returns ':' when ostr begins with ':' and otherwise prints a diagnostic when opterr is non-zero and returns '?'. For a letter without an argument it sets optarg to NULL, advances optind when the element is exhausted, and returns the letter.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): opterr is only read, optreset is cleared; R1/R2 (-1 for '-' not in ostr, optind not advanced) RIGHT and already covered

name: opt_peep
prose: static void opt_peep(opt_state_t *opt_state, struct block *b) in libpcap optimize.c (lines 889-1177). Precondition: b->stmts is a (possibly empty) statement list, b->out_use, b->val, b->s and opt_state->vmap describe the block as computed by the optimizer. Postcondition: returns nothing; if b->stmts is NULL it returns at once. Otherwise it scans pairs of consecutive non-NOP statements s and next, remembering the last real statement, and rewrites in place: 'st M[k]; ldx M[k]' makes the ldx a tax; 'ld #k; tax' becomes 'ldx #k; txa'; and for 'ld #k' followed, optionally after an ldxms, by addx, tax and an indirect load, provided X is not in b->out_use, it adds k to the indirect load's offset and turns the ld, addx and tax into NOPs. If the block's test is 'jeq #k' and A is not in b->out_use, a preceding 'sub x' is folded (when X is a known constant its value is added to k, otherwise only when k == 0 the test becomes 'jeq x'), a preceding 'sub #c' is folded into k, and a preceding 'and #c' with k == 0 becomes 'jset #c' with the two branch targets swapped. After that: 'jset #0' makes JT equal JF, and 'jset #0xffffffff' makes JF equal JT; if X is a known constant and the test uses X, the test becomes an immediate comparison with that value; and if A is a known constant and the test uses an immediate, the test result is computed and JT or JF is set to the other branch (default case aborts). Each rewrite in the statement scan and each jeq-folding rewrite sets opt_state->non_branch_movement_performed = 1 and opt_state->done = 0; the jset normalisation and the constant-X conversion do not; the constant-A folding sets them only when JT and JF differed.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): jset #0/#ffffffff and the constant-X conversion do not set the loop flags, and constant-A folding sets them only if JF != JT (lines 1120-1176)

name: pcap_activate_bpf
prose: static int pcap_activate_bpf(pcap_t *p) in libpcap pcap-bpf.c (lines 1882-2782; I read the whole function, but not its helpers). Precondition: p is a pcap_t being activated, with p->opt set by the caller. Postcondition: returns 0, or a positive warning (PCAP_WARNING_PROMISC_NOTSUP when BIOCPROMISC fails), after installing the BPF read/inject/setfilter/setdirection/set_datalink/getnonblock/setnonblock/stats/cleanup operations, or a negative error code (also status codes from helpers) after calling pcap_cleanup_bpf(p) at the 'bad' label. Steps in order: bpf_open (failure -> its code); BIOCVERSION and version check (failure -> PCAP_ERROR with a message); clamp p->snapshot to MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN when <= 0 or larger; strdup the device name (failure -> PCAP_ERROR); uname; platform-specific parts when compiled in: on macOS the monitor-mode checks (some of which return PCAP_ERROR_RFMON_NOTSUP, PCAP_ERROR_NO_SUCH_DEVICE or PCAP_ERROR without writing a message, e.g. lines 1977, 2453) and the 'wlt' device rename, on FreeBSD creation of a 'usbus' interface, and with zero-copy BPF the zbuf setup; otherwise buffer size selection (explicit BIOCSBLEN with bpf_bind, or halving the default size until bpf_bind succeeds, with check_setif_failure, and 'No buffer size worked' when none does); BIOCGDLT and platform DLT mapping; with BIOCGDLTLIST the DLT list is fetched into p->dlt_list/p->dlt_count (failure -> PCAP_ERROR), and on macOS or BSD with the 802.11 ioctls monitor mode is set up (a monitor_mode failure is returned as its code) and the best 802.11 DLT is selected when possible; if the DLT is DLT_EN10MB with no list a two-entry list {DLT_EN10MB, DLT_DOCSIS} is allocated; p->fddipad and p->linktype are set; BIOCSHDRCMPLT; the read timeout with BIOCSRTIMEOUT (a failure reports PCAP_ERROR; the two error calls there pass errno and PCAP_ERRBUF_SIZE in the opposite order from the other error calls); BIOCIMMEDIATE (or 'Immediate mode not supported'); promiscuous mode (failure only a warning); BIOCSTSTAMP; BIOCGBLEN into p->bufsize and malloc of p->buffer (not in zero-copy mode); an accept-everything filter with the snapshot length through BIOCSETF; selectable_fd is the BPF fd except on FreeBSD 4.3/4.4 where it is -1. Failures write a message to p->errbuf in nearly every case, but several RFMON_NOTSUP returns write none.
note: slice cut head (function begins at 1882); old action was fix with partial prose; reviewer R17 RIGHT: the macOS RFMON_NOTSUP paths set status without writing errbuf

name: pcap_activate_dlpi
prose: static int pcap_activate_dlpi(pcap_t *p) in libpcap pcap-dlpi.c (lines 647-1011). Precondition: p is a DLPI pcap handle with options set; the caller keeps ownership. Postcondition: returns 0 or PCAP_WARNING on success after installing the DLPI read/inject/setfilter (pcapint_install_bpf_program)/nonblock/stats/cleanup operations (set_datalink_op and setdirection_op are NULL) and setting selectable_fd = p->fd; returns a negative status after calling pcap_cleanup_dlpi(p) (the 'bad' label) on failure. Steps: open_dlpi_device (its error code on failure); on HP-UX a second descriptor; DL_INFO request/ack (failure -> PCAP_ERROR); for a style-2 provider dl_doattach (its code); monitor mode requested -> PCAP_ERROR_RFMON_NOTSUP; optional passive mode; the bind (platform-specific; failure -> PCAP_ERROR); clamp the snapshot to MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN; on Solaris ATM a special promiscuous request (failure -> PCAP_ERROR), otherwise with promiscuous mode requested DL_PROMISC_PHYS (failure -> PCAP_ERROR_PROMISC_PERM_DENIED when the code is PCAP_ERROR_PERM_DENIED, else that code) and a DL_PROMISC_MULTI request whose failure only sets status PCAP_WARNING; then DL_PROMISC_SAP (platform-dependent): its failure sets PCAP_WARNING when promiscuous mode was on and otherwise is fatal with the returned code; HP-UX delayed bind; a second DL_INFO and pcap_process_mactype (failure -> PCAP_ERROR); DLIOCRAW where defined (failure -> PCAP_ERROR with a message); bufmod setup with pcap_conf_bufmod (on old Solaris with the known bufmod bug the snapshot is ignored and status becomes PCAP_WARNING with a message); I_FLUSH of the read side (failure -> PCAP_ERROR); pcap_alloc_databuf (failure -> PCAP_ERROR). A warning status is the value returned in the end, so the success return is 0 or PCAP_WARNING, not only 0.
note: old action dropped; real function pcap_activate_dlpi (line 648); I read the whole function; old prose omitted the monitor-mode refusal, the multicast warning and several failure codes

name: pcap_read_linux_mmap_v3
prose: static int pcap_read_linux_mmap_v3(pcap_t *handle, int max_packets, pcap_handler callback, u_char *user) (libpcap pcap-linux.c lines 4460-4595; slice cut head). Precondition: handle is a Linux capture handle using a TPACKET_V3 ring. Postcondition: it returns the number of packets handed to the callback (non-negative), PCAP_ERROR_BREAK, or an error value. If there is no current packet and the current frame is kernel-owned it calls pcap_wait_for_frames_mmap and returns its result when that is non-zero; if the frame is still kernel-owned afterwards (pkts is 0 at this point) it jumps back to wait again when handlep->timeout is 0, otherwise returns 0. An unlimited max_packets is clipped to INT_MAX. In the main loop, for each block owned by userland it processes up to the remaining packet count by calling pcap_handle_packet_mmap per packet (a return of 1 counts the packet, 0 skips a filtered packet, a negative value sets current_packet to NULL and is returned at once without releasing the block). When all packets of a block have been consumed it releases the block to the kernel, decrements blocks_to_filter_in_userland (clearing filter_in_userland when it reaches 0), advances handle->offset (wrapping at handle->cc) and clears current_packet. After each pass, if handle->break_loop is set it clears it and returns PCAP_ERROR_BREAK (even if packets were already delivered in this call). When the loop ends because max_packets was reached or the next block is kernel-owned, it returns pkts, except that if pkts is 0 and timeout is 0 it goes back to wait and retry.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): when packets were read and the next frame is kernel-owned the code returns pkts (lines 4513-4514, 4590-4594), not 0; old prose was inconsistent

name: pcap_activate_npf
prose: static int pcap_activate_npf(pcap_t *p) in libpcap pcap-npf.c (lines 1025-1642; slice cut head and tail; I read the whole function but not the helpers). Precondition: p is a handle whose private data pw is allocated and whose options are set. Postcondition: it first handles monitor mode: if p->opt.rfmon is set and monitor mode is not already on it tries to switch it on, returning PCAP_ERROR_RFMON_NOTSUP (device reports unsupported) or PCAP_ERROR with pw->rfmon_selfstart = 0, otherwise recording rfmon_selfstart = 1; it initialises Winsock, opens the adapter and on failure returns PCAP_ERROR_NO_SUCH_DEVICE (ERROR_BAD_UNIT, errbuf emptied), PCAP_ERROR_PERM_DENIED (ERROR_ACCESS_DENIED, with an explanatory message) or PCAP_ERROR (other errors, undoing a self-started monitor mode); these returns do not call the cleanup. After the adapter is open, any later failure goes to the 'bad' label, which calls pcap_cleanup_npf(p) and returns PCAP_ERROR regardless of the earlier more specific status. It reads the network type (failure -> bad), sets p->linktype from the NDIS medium (Ethernet gets a {DLT_EN10MB, DLT_DOCSIS} list allocated, failure -> bad; an unknown medium selects DLT_EN10MB with a warning message and status PCAP_WARNING), sets the timestamp mode for the host/low-resolution/high-resolution timestamp types when supported (failure -> bad), sets nanosecond mode when requested (failure -> bad), queries the VLAN BPF extension (a failure only writes an errbuf message), clamps the snapshot, sets the hardware filter for promiscuous or non-promiscuous mode (ignoring ERROR_NOT_SUPPORTED-style errors; other failures -> bad), sets the kernel buffer size, allocates p->buffer and sets the minimum-to-copy size for ordinary adapters (failures -> bad; DAG cards go to bad when DAG support is not built), installs an accept-everything BPF program with the snapshot length (failure -> bad), sets the read timeout, optionally disables loopback capture (failure -> bad), installs the NPF read, inject, setfilter and other operations, sets p->handle, and returns status (0, or PCAP_WARNING for an unknown medium).
note: old action was drop with a name 'pcap_activate_win32'; the real function is pcap_activate_npf (line 1026); old prose stopped at the timestamp mode and missed several failure paths

name: snf_activate
prose: static int snf_activate(pcap_t *p) in libpcap pcap-snf.c (lines 240-335). Precondition: p->priv is an initialised struct pcap_snf with snf_boardnum set. Postcondition: returns -1 with a message in p->errbuf if opt.device is NULL ('device is NULL'), if snf_open fails ('snf_open failed'), if snf_ring_open_id fails, or if snf_start fails; in the last two cases the SNF handle (and ring) opened by the earlier steps stay open in ps, and because cleanup_op is only installed after snf_start succeeds, this function does not release them. It first reads the environment: a non-empty SNF_FLAGS gives the open flags, otherwise SNF_NUM_RINGS > 1 selects SNF_F_PSHARED; SNF_PCAP_RING_ID chooses the ring id (default -1). The data ring size passed to snf_open is the buffer size, raised to 1048576 if it is positive but smaller. After the ring is opened it clamps p->snapshot to MAXIMUM_SNAPLEN when <= 0 or larger, sets ps->snf_timeout to -1 when the timeout is <= 0 and to p->opt.timeout otherwise, and starts SNF. On success it sets selectable_fd to -1 (not on Windows), linktype DLT_EN10MB, installs read, inject, setfilter (pcapint_install_bpf_program), set_datalink, getnonblock, setnonblock, stats and cleanup operations (setdirection_op is NULL), clears snf_inj when the inject API exists, and returns 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): cleanup_op is installed only at the end (line 330), so early failures leak the opened handle/ring

name: SWAPSHORT
note: SWAPSHORT is a function-like macro in pcap-util.h (lines 46-48), not a function

name: pcap_parse_source
prose: static int pcap_parse_source(const char *source, char **schemep, char **userinfop, char **hostp, char **portp, char **pathp, char *ebuf) in libpcap pcap.c (lines 1771-2116; the packet showed only the middle of it and called it an unnamed uri parser). Precondition: the five out-pointers and ebuf are writable. Postcondition: if source is NULL or empty it returns -1 with a message in ebuf and leaves the out-parameters untouched (they are set to NULL only after these two checks). Otherwise all five are set to NULL and: with no ':' in source, or a ':' not followed by '//', *pathp is a strdup of the whole source and 0 is returned (malloc failure -> -1 with a message). For a 'file' scheme (case-insensitive) *schemep is the scheme and *pathp is everything after 'file://'. For rpcap or rpcaps with no '/' after the '//', *pathp is everything after '://' and *schemep stays NULL. Otherwise it takes the authority up to the next '/', splits off 'userinfo@' if present, then the host: an IP literal in brackets (the host is returned without the brackets; a missing ']' or extra text after it other than ':' fails with a message) or everything up to ':'; the port is the rest after ':' (it may be an empty string); an empty host part gives NULL host and port. The path is everything after the '/' that ended the authority (empty string if none). On success it returns 0 with *schemep, *pathp allocated and *userinfop, *hostp, *portp each NULL or allocated (the caller frees); on any failure it returns -1 with a message in ebuf, frees every string it had allocated, and leaves the out-parameters NULL.
note: slice shows only lines 1795-2062; real function pcap_parse_source (line 1772); old prose wrongly said the out-parameters are first set to NULL in the NULL/empty-source error cases (they are untouched)

name: daemon_msg_startcap_req
prose: static int daemon_msg_startcap_req(uint8 ver, struct daemon_slpars *pars, uint32 plen, char *source, struct session **sessionp, struct rpcap_sampling *samp_param, int uses_ssl) in libpcap rpcapd/daemon.c (lines 1953-2293; slice cut head). Precondition: the control connection pars is open and the request's remaining payload length is plen. Postcondition: it receives the start-capture request (a fatal receive error jumps to fatal_error; a non-fatal one to error), rejects a datagram request when SSL is in use, allocates a session, opens the capture device with pcap_open_live, then creates the data socket either actively (connecting to the client's address and port) or passively (listening on a free port), unpacks and applies the client's filter (-1 -> fatal_error, -2 -> error), sends the start-capture reply carrying the buffer size and, for passive mode, the port (a send failure goes to fatal_error), accepts the client's data connection in passive mode, performs the TLS handshake on the data socket when uses_ssl, starts the data thread, and discards any excess request data (failure -> fatal_error). On full success it returns 0 with *sessionp pointing at the new session. In the 'error' path (non-fatal errors) it sets *sessionp = NULL, frees addrinfo and the session, sends the client an error reply (PCAP_ERR_STARTCAPTURE with the message in errmsgbuf; several error sites fill errbuf instead, so the reply can carry an uninitialised or stale message) and discards excess data; it returns 0 if both succeed, or -1 if sending the error reply or discarding the data fails. In the 'fatal_error' path it sets *sessionp = NULL, closes and frees any session, sends no error reply and returns -1.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): -1 is also returned from the error path when sending the error reply or discarding data fails, after an error reply was attempted; fatal_error itself sends none; also noted errmsgbuf/errbuf mismatch

name: pcap_next_packet
prose: static int pcap_next_packet(pcap_t *p, struct pcap_pkthdr *hdr, u_char **data) (libpcap sf-pcap.c lines 517-789; slice cut head). Precondition: p->rfile is positioned at a per-packet header; hdr and data are non-NULL. Postcondition: returns 0 only at a clean end of file (no bytes read for the header; hdr and data untouched); returns -1 with a message in p->errbuf on a header read I/O error, a truncated header, a captured length above max_snaplen_for_dlt(linktype) (the message mentions the snapshot length or the maximum), buffer growth failure, or an I/O error or EOF while reading the packet bytes or the bytes beyond the snapshot length; in the error cases *hdr may already be partly filled and *data is not set. On success it returns 1: hdr is filled from the file header (byte-swapped when p->swapped, microseconds scaled to nanoseconds or the reverse according to scale_type, caplen and len exchanged when lengths_swapped is SWAPPED, or MAYBE_SWAPPED with caplen > len); if caplen exceeds the snapshot length the buffer is grown to the snapshot length, the first snapshot bytes are read, the rest is read and discarded in 4096-byte pieces and caplen is set to the snapshot length; otherwise the buffer is grown (next power of two, capped at the snapshot length) if needed and caplen bytes are read. *data is set to p->buffer and pcapint_post_process(linktype, swapped, hdr, data) is called before returning. p->buffer may be reallocated, so earlier pointers into it become invalid.
note: reviewer WRONG (R15): pcapint_post_process IS called at line 786

name: kh_resize_##name
prose: Macro-generated function kh_resize_##name(kh_##name##_t *h, khint_t new_n_buckets), defined inside __KHASH_IMPL in khash.h (lines 244-~310). Precondition: h is a valid initialised table of the generated type. Postcondition: new_n_buckets is rounded up to a power of two (minimum 4). If h->size is at least (khint_t)(new_n_buckets * 0.77 + 0.5) no rehash is done and the table is left unchanged. Otherwise it allocates and fills a new flags array (failure -> -1), and when growing reallocates the keys array (and the values array for maps); a failure frees the new flags and returns -1, with h->keys possibly already enlarged (valid, contents preserved) if only the values reallocation failed. It then rehashes every live element into the new capacity with the kick-out scheme, shrinks the keys and values arrays when shrinking (these shrinking reallocations are not checked), frees the old flags, installs the new flags and n_buckets, and (in the part after the slice) updates n_occupied and upper_bound; it returns 0 in the success and no-op cases. The caller keeps ownership of h.
note: added: shrink reallocations unchecked; verified lines 244-302 of the macro

name: TREE_ROTL_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_ROTL_##node##_##field(struct node *self) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_ROTL_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self and self->avl_right are non-NULL and the subtrees have valid heights. Postcondition: the right child r becomes the new subtree root: self takes over r's former left subtree, self is rebalanced with TREE_BALANCE and becomes r's left child, then r is rebalanced and returned as the new root. Rebalancing recomputes heights and may rotate further.

name: TREE_ROTR_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_ROTR_##node##_##field(struct node *self) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_ROTR_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self and self->avl_left are non-NULL and the subtrees have valid heights. Postcondition: the left child l becomes the new subtree root: self takes over l's former right subtree, self is rebalanced and becomes l's right child, then l is rebalanced and returned as the new root.

name: TREE_BALANCE_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_BALANCE_##node##_##field(struct node *self) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_BALANCE_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self is non-NULL and its children are valid subtrees with correct heights. Postcondition: it computes delta = (left height) - (right height), where a missing child counts as 0. If delta < -1 it first rotates the right child to the right when that child leans left (delta of the child > 0), then rotates self left and returns the new root; if delta > 1 it first rotates the left child left when that child leans right, then rotates self right and returns the new root; otherwise it sets self's avl_height to 1 plus the larger child height and returns self.

name: TREE_INSERT_##node##_##field

Precondition: elm is non-NULL with its child pointers NULL and a valid avl_height (this function does not initialise them), compare is a valid ordering, and self is a valid AVL subtree or NULL. Postcondition: if self is NULL it returns elm; otherwise it recursively inserts elm into the left subtree when compare(elm, self) < 0, else into the right subtree (so elements that compare equal go right), and returns self after TREE_BALANCE.

name: TREE_REMOVE_##node##_##field
prose: Macro-generated function TREE_REMOVE_##node##_##field(struct node *self, struct node *elm, int (*compare)(struct node *, struct node *)) defined inside TREE_DEFINE(node, field) in libucl tree.h (the real name is TREE_REMOVE_<node>_<field>). Precondition: self is a valid AVL subtree or NULL and compare is consistent with the tree's ordering. Postcondition: returns NULL if self is NULL. If compare(elm, self) == 0 it detaches self: its left subtree and right subtree are merged with TREE_MOVE_RIGHT (the right subtree is attached at the rightmost position of the left subtree, rebalancing along that path), self's avl_left and avl_right are set to NULL (its height is not reset) and the merged subtree root is returned. Otherwise it recurses into the left subtree when compare(elm, self) < 0, else the right, and returns self after TREE_BALANCE. The node matched is the one whose compare result is 0, which need not be the same pointer as elm; nothing is freed.

name: ucl_msgpack_consume
prose: static bool ucl_msgpack_consume(struct ucl_parser *parser) in libucl ucl_msgpack.c (lines 947-1330; the packet called it an unnamed parse loop; I read the whole function, but only skimmed the sub-parsers it calls). Precondition: parser->chunks->begin/remain describe the msgpack buffer. Postcondition: it runs a state machine over the buffer (read_type, start_assoc, start_array, read_assoc_key, read_assoc_value, read_array_value, finish states). It returns false, in every such case with parser->err set (ucl_create_err or inside the called helpers), for: an unknown msgpack type byte; not enough data for a length field; an invalid length-field size; a failure of ucl_msgpack_insert_object (no key for an object member, bad container type); a NULL result of ucl_msgpack_get_container (out of memory or a bad top-level object); a negative result from a sub-parser (the CONSUME_RET macro); a key whose type is not a string, or an empty or too long key; a value or container operation with no container on the stack; an empty container found by GET_NEXT_STATE; the error state; at the end of input, a non-empty container still starting, an unfinished value, an invalid finishing state, or a non-empty stack after rewinding ('incomplete container'). It returns true only if the whole buffer was consumed without these errors and the container stack is empty after the final rewind. In the final handling of a trailing empty container the return value of the sub-parser is not checked.
note: reviewer WRONG (R17): the NULL-container and insert failures do set parser->err (ucl_msgpack_get_container lines 777-779, 787-789, 816; ucl_msgpack_insert_object lines 855-857, 869)

name: ucl_state_machine
prose: static bool ucl_state_machine(struct ucl_parser *parser) in libucl ucl_parser.c (lines 2424-2770; slice cut head). Precondition: parser->chunks is the chunk to parse. Postcondition: if parser->top_obj is NULL the state is reset to UCL_STATE_INIT. It loops while chunk->pos < chunk->end handling the states INIT, KEY/KEY_OBRACE, VALUE, AFTER_VALUE, MACRO_NAME, MACRO and ERROR. It returns true at once from the AFTER_VALUE state when ucl_parse_after_value succeeded and the object stack is empty (the rest of the chunk is ignored); otherwise after the loop it attaches any pending last comment to the current, stacked or top object (or drops it), and then, if the stack is non-empty and the state is not ERROR, it checks the stack entries belonging to this chunk for open braces: if any was opened with a brace it appends 'unmatched open brace' text to parser->err, sets err_code to UCL_EUNPAIRED and returns false; otherwise it returns true. It returns false after setting parser->state to UCL_STATE_ERROR (and, in most cases, an error message) for: a failed comment skip or syntax error in INIT, a key where the stack is already empty, a failure of ucl_parse_key, ucl_parse_value (or a NULL current object, which sets the state but no message), ucl_parse_after_value, an invalid, unknown or malformed macro, a failure of ucl_parse_macro_value, an unknown state (internal-error message), or the error state itself. It also returns false without changing the state when creating a container fails (INIT or nested key case), and when a macro handler returns false (the state was already restored from prev_state; a missing macro sets an internal error message).
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 (container allocation failures return false without setting UCL_STATE_ERROR) and R15 (UCL_STATE_VALUE with a NULL cur_obj returns false without a message, lines 2559-2563)

name: ucl_schema_validate
prose: static bool ucl_schema_validate(const ucl_object_t *schema, const ucl_object_t *obj, bool try_array, struct ucl_schema_error *err, const ucl_object_t *root, ucl_object_t *external_refs) in libucl ucl_schema.c (lines 929-1066; slice cut head). Precondition: schema and root are valid; obj is non-NULL unless try_array is true; err may be NULL, but if the schema contains a satisfied 'anyOf' or a failing 'not' subschema the code writes err->code, so err must then be non-NULL. Postcondition: returns false with UCL_SCHEMA_INVALID_SCHEMA if schema is not an object. With try_array true it checks maxValues and minValues over the sibling chain starting at obj (a violation gives UCL_SCHEMA_CONSTRAINT and false) and validates every element of that chain individually (try_array false), returning true if all pass. With try_array false it checks, in order: 'enum'; 'allOf' (each sub-schema validated with try_array true; the first failure returns false); 'anyOf' (the first sub-schema that passes ends the loop, a pass sets err->code = UCL_SCHEMA_OK, no pass returns false with the last sub-validation's error left in err; note that for an empty anyOf array 'ret' is read uninitialised); 'oneOf' (false if no sub-schema or more than one passes; when more than one passes no new error is written); 'not' (false if the subschema passes, without writing an error; if it fails err->code is reset to UCL_SCHEMA_OK); '$ref' (resolved through ucl_schema_resolve_ref, false on failure, then validated with the referenced schema); the 'type' constraint (false on mismatch); and finally returns the result of the object, array, number (int or float) or string validators according to obj->type, or true for other types.
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 (not/oneOf failures do not set err) and R15 (err->code is dereferenced in the anyOf success and not branches, so err may not be NULL there, lines 994, 1023)

name: ucl_load_handler
prose: bool ucl_load_handler(const unsigned char *data, size_t len, const ucl_object_t *args, void *ud) in libucl ucl_util.c (lines 1771-1930; slice cut head). Precondition: ud is the parser; when len > 0 the stack must be non-empty (parser->stack->obj is used without a check). Postcondition: returns false (no message) if parser is NULL. It reads options from args when args is an object: booleans try, multiline, escape, trim (matched with strncmp against the key's length, so a key that is a prefix of an option name also matches), strings key and target, integer priority. It returns false with message 'No Key specified in load macro' if key is NULL or empty. If len is 0 it returns false with 'Unable to parse load macro'. Otherwise it copies the file name (allocation failure -> false) and fetches the file with ucl_fetch_file: on failure it returns try_load (true when try was set, after clearing the error; false otherwise with the error left in parser->err). If the top container already has the key it sets 'Key %s already exists', unmaps the buffer and returns false. For target 'string' (case-insensitive, the default) it creates a string object from the buffer with the escape/trim flags, copies its value, and sets the multiline flag if requested; if object creation returns NULL these later steps use the NULL pointer without a check. For target 'int' it copies the buffer to a temporary string (allocation failure -> false, with a message, buffer unmapped), parses it with strtoll base 10 and creates an integer object. Any other target creates no object. It unmaps the buffer and, if an object was created, sets its key and priority and inserts it into the top container, then returns true (also when no object was created).
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the string branch dereferences the object returned by ucl_object_fromstring_common without a NULL check (lines 1887-1891), so 'returns true when object creation fails' is not what the code does

name: cbor_handler
prose: static int cbor_handler(XO_ENCODER_HANDLER_ARGS) in libxo enc_cbor.c (lines 243-102 of the excerpt; real function at lines 243-343; slice cut head). Precondition: xop is a valid handle; unless op is XO_OP_CREATE the private data (the cbor_private_t) must exist; name and value must be valid strings for the ops that use them. Postcondition: if XOF_PRETTY is set it first prints a trace line ('op <name>: [name] [value]') and flushes stdout, even when there is no private data. name: csv_open_level
prose: static int csv_open_level(xo_handle_t *xop, csv_private_t *csv, const char *name, int instance) in libxo enc_csv.c (lines 420-457). Precondition: csv is a valid csv_private_t with its path and name stack initialised; name is a valid string. xop is marked UNUSED in the parameter list but is in fact used: it is passed to csv_emit_record and csv_dbg. name: xo_set_options
prose: int xo_set_options(xo_handle_t *xop, const char *input) in libxo libxo.c (lines 2261-2443; slice cut head). Precondition: xop may be NULL (the default handle is used). Postcondition: if input is NULL it returns 0 and changes nothing. If input starts with ':' each following character is a one-letter option (c f F g H I i<digits> J k n P T U u W X x set the corresponding flag, style or indent; other letters are ignored) and it returns 0. Otherwise it works on a copy and processes comma-separated tokens: '@name' and 'encoder=name' call xo_encoder_init (a missing name calls xo_failure, a failed init issues a warning, and in both cases rc is assigned the init result); 'colors=...' sets the colour map; a style name is accepted only the first time (the first style wins and later ones are ignored with a warning) and is applied after the loop only if it is greater than 0; other names are looked up as flags (set), 'no-color' (clears colour), 'indent=N' (a missing value calls xo_failure); any other token warns 'unknown libxo option value' and sets rc to -1. It returns rc, which is 0 if nothing failed, -1 after an unknown token, or the last xo_encoder_init result; a later successful encoder initialisation overwrites an earlier -1 with 0.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): the first style wins (line 2408-2411) and a later 'rc = xo_encoder_init()' can overwrite an earlier -1

name: xo_do_format_field
prose: static ssize_t xo_do_format_field(xo_handle_t *xop, xo_buffer_t *xbp, const char *fmt, ssize_t flen, xo_xff_flags_t flags) in libxo libxo.c (lines 3309-3664; slice cut head). Precondition: xop->xo_vap holds the arguments for fmt, fmt has flen readable bytes, xbp is NULL (then xo_data is used) or a writable buffer. Postcondition: returns 0 when the whole format was processed, and -1 when a format has too many '.' qualifiers, contains an 'n' or 'v' conversion, or xo_buf_has_room fails for the per-field format copy. It walks fmt: literal runs (with '%%' and backslash escapes) are appended through xo_format_string_direct when output is wanted; each conversion is parsed into an xo_format_t, a '%@...@' prefix is skipped (a '*' inside it consumes an int argument unless XOF_NO_VA_ARG), and the field is skipped (no output) when XFF_NO_OUTPUT is set or when a hidden-field flag does not apply to the style (the tests use XOF_ISSET on the handle with XFF constants). If not skipped, string conversions (s, S, m) with no formatter go through xo_format_string and others through xo_vsnprintf with escaping appropriate to XML, HTML, JSON, SDPARAMS or encoder styles; xo_columns and xo_anchor_columns are updated when XOF_COLUMNS and XOIF_ANCHOR are set. Unless XOF_NO_VA_ARG is set, the corresponding va_arg arguments are consumed for every conversion (also for skipped fields; for a skipped 's' the string pointer is popped), so XFF_NO_OUTPUT suppresses output but not argument consumption, whereas XOF_NO_VA_ARG suppresses consumption. A missing conversion character only reports xo_failure and continues. After the loop the trailing literal is appended, and with the gettext flags xo_format_gettext post-processes the field.
note: reviewer R15 partly WRONG: with XFF_NO_OUTPUT (make_output false) no output is appended but va_arg arguments are still consumed (lines 3400, 3566-3629); only XOF_NO_VA_ARG avoids consuming

name: xo_do_close_container
prose: static int xo_do_close_container(xo_handle_t *xop, const char *name) in libxo libxo.c (lines 7043-7102; slice cut head). Precondition: xop may be NULL (the default handle is used). Postcondition: if name is NULL it is taken from the top stack entry (copied into an alloca buffer because xo_depth_change frees it); if that entry has no name and lacks XSF_DTRT a failure is reported and XO_FAILURE_NAME is used, while in DTRT mode with no stack name it stays NULL. By style: XML calls xo_depth_change (depth -1, indent -1) and prints the closing tag, returning the number of bytes printed; JSON sets the stack flags, changes depth and indent by -1, prints '}' (with newlines if pretty), marks the enclosing stack entry XSF_NOT_FIRST and returns the printed byte count; HTML and TEXT change the depth by -1 (indent unchanged) and print nothing (return 0); SDPARAMS does nothing at all, including no depth change (return 0); ENCODER changes the depth by -1 and returns xo_encoder_handle's result for XO_OP_CLOSE_CONTAINER.
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 (xop may be NULL; DTRT keeps name NULL) and R15 (SDPARAMS does not decrement depth, line 7092-7093)

name: xo_do_close
prose: static int xo_do_close(xo_handle_t *xop, const char *name, xo_state_t new_state) in libxo libxo.c (lines 7597-7656; slice cut head). Precondition: xop is valid. Postcondition: new_state is mapped to the open state that must be found (container, list, instance, leaf list) or, for XSS_MARKER, a marker; any other new_state returns 0 at once. It scans the stack from the top entry down (never reaching entry 0). When need_state is not a marker and it meets a marker: if name is non-NULL it reports a failure and returns 0; otherwise it reports 'close stops at marker', uses that marker as the limit and stops. When looking for a marker (new_state XSS_MARKER) markers do not stop the scan. An entry matches when its state equals the needed state and, when name is non-NULL, its name is NULL or equal to name (entries without a name are not skipped). If no limit was found it reports a failure and returns 0. Otherwise it returns xo_do_close_all(xop, limit), which closes every scope from the top down to and including the limit and always returns 0 (a negative close result is only reported with xo_failure). So the function returns 0 on every path.
note: reviewer RIGHT (R15): a marker does not stop the scan when new_state is XSS_MARKER, and entries with no name match any name (lines 7622, 7640)

name: xo_transition
prose: static ssize_t xo_transition(xo_handle_t *xop, xo_xof_flags_t flags, const char *name, xo_state_t new_state) in libxo libxo.c (lines 7661-7919; the slice ends at line 7903, before the flush handling). Precondition: xop may be NULL (xo_default is used); the stack is initialised. Postcondition: it finds the effective old state (skipping markers on top of the stack, remembering that it started on a marker) and dispatches on the pair (old state, new state): it opens or closes containers, lists, instances and leaf lists through the xo_do_* functions, first closing an open list or leaf list or instance when needed, returns the result of the last such call (negative on its failure), does nothing (rc 0) for the emit transitions that need nothing, logs a failure and does nothing for close-instance and close-leaf-list from the initial state, and logs 'unknown transition' for unlisted pairs (rc stays 0). If a close would have to cross a marker it logs a failure and returns -1 at once, without setting XOIF_MADE_OUTPUT. Otherwise, after the dispatch, if rc is non-negative and XOF_FLUSH is set it calls xo_flush_h and returns -1 if that fails; it then sets XOIF_MADE_OUTPUT (also when rc is negative) and returns rc.

name: yaml_parser_load_mapping
prose: static int yaml_parser_load_mapping(yaml_parser_t *parser, yaml_event_t *event, struct loader_ctx *ctx) in libyaml loader.c (lines 482-527; slice shows lines 505-544; the packet named it yaml_parser_load_mapping_start). Precondition: event is a MAPPING-START event whose tag and anchor strings are handed over to this function. Postcondition: it checks the document node stack limit, replaces a NULL tag or a '!' tag by a copy of the default mapping tag, creates an empty pairs stack and a mapping node that owns the tag and pairs, pushes the node on parser->document->nodes, registers the anchor for the new node index, records the node in its parent with yaml_parser_load_node_add, checks the loader-context stack limit and pushes the index onto *ctx; it returns 1 on success. It returns 0 on failure: if the node-stack limit check, the default tag duplication, the pairs stack initialisation, or the push of the node onto the document nodes fails, it frees the tag and the event's anchor and returns 0 (a pairs stack already allocated is not freed on the push-failure path); if registering the anchor, load_node_add, the context limit check or the context push fails after the node was pushed, it returns 0 without freeing the tag (now owned by the node on the document's node stack), with the anchor handled by yaml_parser_register_anchor, and with nothing pushed onto *ctx unless the last push itself succeeded.
note: slice cut head; real function name yaml_parser_load_mapping (line 483); old prose slightly overstated that nothing was pushed to ctx on every failure after the node push - only the final push can succeed or fail last

name: yaml_parser_parse_flow_mapping_value
prose: static int yaml_parser_parse_flow_mapping_value(yaml_parser_t *parser, yaml_event_t *event, int empty) in libyaml parser.c (lines 1169-1199). Precondition: a token can be peeked from the scanner. Postcondition: returns 0 if no token can be peeked (error set by the scanner). If empty is non-zero it sets parser->state to YAML_PARSE_FLOW_MAPPING_KEY_STATE and returns the result of yaml_parser_process_empty_scalar (1 with an empty plain scalar event at the token's start mark, or 0 with YAML_MEMORY_ERROR if allocation fails). Otherwise, if the token is a VALUE token it is skipped and the next token is peeked (failure -> 0); if that token is neither a FLOW-ENTRY nor a FLOW-MAPPING-END it pushes YAML_PARSE_FLOW_MAPPING_KEY_STATE on the parser's states stack (failure -> 0) and returns yaml_parser_parse_node(parser, event, 0, 0), which determines parser->state itself (for a plain scalar the pushed state is restored later, for a collection the state becomes the first-entry state of that collection). In the remaining cases (no VALUE token, or the VALUE is followed directly by a flow entry or mapping end) it sets parser->state to YAML_PARSE_FLOW_MAPPING_KEY_STATE and returns the empty scalar event as above.
note: reviewers RIGHT: R1 and R15 (the node branch leaves the state to parse_node, not FLOW_MAPPING_KEY_STATE)
